s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, with progression to foot drop, without significant low back pain
salient_findings: Foot drop with significant weakness of tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus
key_facts: 48-year-old woman with a history of asthma
2-day history of right lower-extremity numbness and pain
Denies any low back pain
Manual muscle testing of the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus was 3/5
Gastrocnemius and flexor hallucis longus were 4/5
Deep-tendon reflexes were normal
Straight-leg-raising was positive at 70 degrees
Femoral-nerve stretch test was negative
Degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1 on plain radiographs
Right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 without significant nerve-root or cord compression on lumbar MRI
Initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
Ankle-brachial indices were decreased
Lower-extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
Muscle strength nearly normalized by day 7, but lateral leg pain persisted
Pain increased by day 22, and right foot drop developed by day 26
Urgent MRI showed no new nerve-root compression
Repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential

shortlist.label: L5 radiculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness with progression to foot drop, consistent with L5 nerve root involvement

shortlist.label: Peroneal nerve palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Foot drop and weakness in muscles innervated by the peroneal nerve, consistent with peroneal nerve palsy

shortlist.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness with progression to foot drop, consistent with lumbosacral plexus involvement

shortlist.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness, with decreased ankle-brachial indices, raising suspicion for vasculitic neuropathy

shortlist.label: Idiopathic lumbosacral plexitis
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral lower extremity numbness, pain, and weakness with progression to foot drop, without a clear alternative diagnosis, consistent with idiopathic lumbosacral plexitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of right lower-extremity numbness and pain, particularly the involvement of the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus muscles, along with the development of right foot drop, are consistent with peroneal nerve palsy. The initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies showing a decreased motor conduction velocity and the repeat studies failing to elicit an evoked myogenic potential further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: L5 radiculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1, the lack of significant nerve-root compression on MRI and the specific muscle groups affected make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lumbosacral plexopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are more localized to the peroneal nerve distribution, rather than a more widespread involvement of the lumbosacral plexus.

rejected.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of vasculitis or systemic inflammation in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Idiopathic lumbosacral plexitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic findings are more consistent with a specific nerve injury, rather than an idiopathic plexitis.
